text:
ana: quick note while porting the sample app from Python -> Go: found a parity/ergonomics oddity in the Go generator iterator around context cancellation and auth refresh. Wanted to get thoughts before filing a formal proposal.

ben: curious, what's different from Python's behavior?

ana: (typo) ana: in Python we use a streaming callback with an explicit cancel token and the SDK cancels internal retries when the user cancels. In Go, we rely on context propagation and the Next(ctx) pull pattern. When an auth refresh happens mid-stream, cancelling ctx returns from Next, but an internal retry goroutine (spawned by our auth helper/transport) sometimes keeps retrying and doesn't stop.

charlie: can you paste a minimal repro + logs? even a short sketch helps.

ana: simplified repro: create a short deadline ctx, use a fake auth provider that sleeps 700-900ms on refresh, call iter.Next(ctx) in the usual for-loop. Cancel happens while refresh is in-flight. Observed: Next returns, iter.Err() shows deadline, but logs keep printing "auth: refresh start" afterwards.

Logs:
```
2026-02-14T12:03:00Z auth: refresh start (svc-key)
2026-02-14T12:03:00Z transport: got 401, retrying
2026-02-14T12:03:01Z ctx deadline exceeded
2026-02-14T12:03:02Z auth: refresh start (svc-key)
2026-02-14T12:03:03Z auth: refresh start (svc-key)
```

ana: root cause appears to be twofold: (1) our auth refresh helper spawns a goroutine that isn't tied to the request ctx, (2) transport retry/backoff loops don't always select on ctx.Done() between attempts. Unlike Python's implementation, the Go path has detached background work.

ben: ack. Two levels of fix: short-term DX improvement that doesn't break API, and long-term correctness change.

charlie: proposal for short-term: add io.Closer-style Close() to the iterator returned by client.Generator. Close should signal internal stop channel and wait for workers to drain; make it idempotent and safe to defer. Update sample app quickstart to show `defer iter.Close()`. That gives users an explicit shutdown hook.

ben: sounds good. Long-term: auth refresh helper should accept a context and return when ctx.Done() is observed. Transport retry loops should select on ctx.Done() before each sleep/backoff. That aligns behavior with our other SDKs and prevents detached retries.

ana: additional parity ask: consider adding a GeneratorOptions flag WithExplicitShutdown or having Generator implement context-aware behavior by default. Users coming from Python expect cancel -> stop everything. We should document the Go semantics explicitly.

charlie: we should avoid API churn. Close() + docs now, auth + retry ctx-awareness later, both in the same minor release if possible. Also add a small unit test that injects a slow auth double, cancels ctx, and asserts no lingering auth goroutines after a grace period. Make it eventual-assertion to avoid flakes.

ben: test idea: expose a test hook that returns current active auth worker count so test can reliably wait until zero. No production API change; test-only hook in *_test.go.

ana: for sampleapp onboarding, I suggest we update the Quickstart README with a small callout: "Go generator: prefer defer iter.Close() in addition to cancelling context for short-deadline flows (see FAQ)". That will reduce confusion for newcomers.

charlie: also add a changelog note under SDK: "Go: iterator Close() added to help cancel in-flight generator work; auth refresh will become context-aware in upcoming patch".

doc-bot: opened issue #3198 "go-sdk: generator iterator Close() + auth refresh should honor ctx" (assigned to @charlie).

ci-bot: created PR draft #3240: "devex: sampleapp quickstart - defer iter.Close()" (review requested from @ben).

ana: I'll volunteer to author the flaky-resistant unit test and a small sampleapp patch showing defer iter.Close(). happy to pair on the iterator API impl.

charlie: thanks! i'll prototype Close() as io.Closer, wire it to an internal stop channel, and add godoc recommending `defer iter.Close()` for best-effort early shutdown. We'll follow up with an auth audit and a small opt-in flag for context-aware refresh if we need staged rollout.

ben: nice triage. This will help parity and save users who port from Node/Python. :tada:
